Theme

Latin word

interest

impersonal verb (from intersum): with an indirect question · Wiktionary

it depends (who, what, how, whether …); it makes a difference; there is a difference; it is in the interest of, it matters to

In this lexicon

  • depend

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 6.24.1: Quam multum interest quid ā quōque fīat!; Cic. Fam. 13.10.4: interest quālis prīmus aditus sit

  • difference

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.11: inter hominem et bēluam hoc maximē interest; Ter. Ad. 76: hoc pater ac dominus interest

  • interest

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre; Cic. Fam. 2.4.1; Traupman 101

  • magnī interest: important

    classical

  • Nīl interest.: it makes no difference

    classical

  • is quī interest: participant

    classical

Examples

  • Quam multum interest quid ā quōque fīat!

    How much depends on who does a thing!Plin. Ep. 6.24.1

    In the entry for depend

  • Dī inmortālēs, hominī homō quid praestat? stultō intellegēns quid inter est?

    Good gods, how one man can outdo another! What a difference there is between a fool and a man of sense!Ter. Eun. 232–233

    In the entry for difference

  • Hoc pater ac dominus interest: hoc quī nequit, fateātur nescīre imperāre līberīs.

    That is the difference between a father and a master; whoever can’t do it should admit he doesn’t know how to bring up children.Ter. Ad. 76–77

    In the entry for difference
